subject: Pilot bridge structuring — pricing options and next steps
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@clarityai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot bridge structuring — pricing options and next steps

Hi Samira,

Great to hear the eval is showing traction — thanks for the early signals. Per our call this morning, I wanted to put three concrete options on the table for a short bridge (2–6 weeks) so you can complete the last integration tests without losing momentum. I attached a one-pager and the playbook worksheet.

Summary (high level):
- Option A — Time-box extension (2 weeks): pro-rated seat-based price for the extension period, no credits; we keep existing trial SKU but extend access.
- Option B — Credit top-up: upfront token credit top-up tied to a conversion credit (if you sign a 12 month commit within 60 days, X% of the top-up converts).
- Option C — Burst slab (temporary higher concurrency slab): fixed short-term SKU for increased throughput billed as a separate invoice line (good for spike-heavy tests).

Key asks from your side to pick a path: expected peak concurrent requests during the finish tests, and whether procurement prefers a single amendment invoice or a credit memo.

Attached: rdw_pilot_pricing_options_v2.pdf (summary) and bridge_playbook_v1.docx (worksheet).

If you'd like, Marissa and Karthik will model the economics for each so we can propose an exact dollar figure; otherwise we can send a suggested number by EOD tomorrow.

Next step: pick A/B/C and confirm procurement preference — I can then loop legal for a short amendment.

Thanks,
Irene

-- 
Irene Choi

From: Samira Khan <samira@clarityai.com>

Cc: Ben Holt <ben.holt@clarityai.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot bridge structuring — pricing options and next steps

Irene — thanks for the clear options. A couple of quick clarifications before we pick: 

1) For Option B (credit top-up) — how does the conversion credit work exactly? Is it dollar-for-dollar or a percentage rebate when we move to a committed contract?
2) For Option C — can the burst slab be limited to only the test cluster (so we don't pay for production traffic)?
3) Procurement question: they generally prefer a single amendment invoice rather than a credit memo (keeps accounting tidy). Is that supported?

Ben and I discussed — we lean toward Option B if the conversion credit converts cleanly to committed spend (i.e. applied as a prepayment toward the first invoice). We'd also like a short SLA during the bridge (uptime and response times for the test endpoints).

Could your team sketch the exact numbers so procurement can route the amendment?

Thanks,
Samira

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 11:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot bridge structuring — pricing options and next steps

Samira / team — jumping in with recommended mechanics based on common patterns that work well for evaluations finishing integration tests. I attached a quick workbook with numbers; see the short summary below.

Recommended (we think balances risk & procurement preference):
- Offer: Option B (Credit top-up) as primary.
  - Provide a $15k token credit top-up applied immediately for the bridge (covers expected incremental tokens for experiments).
  - Conversion mechanic: if ClarityAI signs a 12-month commit within 60 days of go‑live, 60% of that $15k converts to a prepayment credit applied to the first committed invoice; 40% is non-refundable (covers immediate infra).
- SLA: 99.5% availability on test endpoints for the bridge window; operational on-call during working hours; escalation route to our CS/Eng.
- Invoice flow: we can do a single amendment invoice (line item: "Pilot bridge credit") which your procurement prefers; we'll also provide a credit memo option if needed for internal accounting — both are possible.

Why this structure: it gives you downside protection (most value applied to a future committed contract) while giving us coverage for the short-term usage spike. The math in the workbook assumes a 2–3 week finish window and a modest extrasurfacing rate.

If you confirm, I'll prepare a clean amendment with the numbers and loop legal. Karthik, can you sanity-check the SLA wording and ensure the conversion credit is represented correctly on the invoice?

Thanks,
Marissa

Attachment: clarity_usage_workbook.xlsx (breakdown & conversion math)

--
Marissa Cole
Director, Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0119

Subject: Re: Pilot bridge structuring — pricing options and next steps

Samira / Ben — thanks for the quick review and the procurement preference — good to know. This is the agreed path unless you flag concerns:

1) We will proceed with Option B: $15k token credit top-up applied immediately as an invoice line item ("Pilot bridge credit").
2) Conversion: 60% of the credit converts to a prepayment credit toward the first 12‑month committed invoice if signed within 60 days; 40% retained as non-refundable bridge fee.
3) SLA: 99.5% availability on the test endpoints during the bridge window; Redwood will provide primary on-call during PST business hours, with an escalation contact listed in the amendment.
4) Invoice format: single amendment invoice preferred; we'll add a separate audit-friendly credit memo if your accounting team requests one.

Next steps from Redwood: Marissa will create the amendment draft (numbers on the invoice) and Karthik will confirm the SLA language. I will send the DocuSign package once legal signs off. Expected turnaround: 48–72 hours.

DocuSign preview: https://app.docusign.com/prepare/RDW-CLARI-042-AMP
Drive folder (playbook & workbook): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cPilotPlaybook

Samira — please confirm the acceptance of Option B and procurement preference for a single amendment invoice and we'll start the paperwork.

Appreciate the quick coordination — excited to keep momentum.

Best,
Irene
